2_Introduction: The champion device showed a PCE of 18.2667%, with JSC of 24.113 mA/cm², FF of 69.0619%, and VOC of 1.0969 V. The Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1 perovskite film was prepared with a concentration of 1.73 mol/L. Afterwards, the perovskite precursor solution was deposited on the substrate via a two-step spin coating process; first, the solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then at 5000 rpm for 30 s. To promote better film morphology, 160 µL of antisolvent was added at last 6 s in the latter spin-coating step. The device architecture benefited from a final anneal at 110 °C for 25 min, ensuring robust crystallinity.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ perovskite layer—engineered with a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture—achieves optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and suppressed halide segregation while maintaining phase stability against δ-phase formation, wherein the partial substitution of FA⁺ with smaller MA⁺ and Cs⁺ enhances lattice rigidity and reduces Pb–I antibonding character at the conduction band minimum, thereby elevating VOC; the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration balances nucleation density and growth kinetics, preventing premature aggregation during the two-step spin-coating protocol—where the initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) step enables uniform wetting and interfacial contact, followed by high-speed (5000 rpm, 30 s) crystallization under controlled shear—and the precisely timed antisolvent quench (160 µL at the final 6 s) triggers instantaneous supersaturation, favoring homogeneous nucleation over Ostwald ripening and yielding densely packed, micron-sized grains with minimized grain boundary area, as corroborated by high-coverage optical micrographs showing >98% film continuity and negligible pinholes, while PL mapping reveals uniformly elevated intensity across the entire active area with a monoexponential decay lifetime of 328 ns—signifying suppressed non-radiative recombination from both bulk and interfacial trap states—and XRD confirms complete elimination of residual PbI₂ (no peak at 12.6°) alongside narrow (001) FAPbI₃ reflections (FWHM = 0.12°) and absence of δ-phase peaks, evidencing full conversion to the photoactive α-phase with minimal microstrain and enhanced structural coherence; this synergistic crystallization control is intrinsically coupled to interfacial energetics and defect passivation, although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators were introduced—implying that the intrinsic stoichiometric precision, cationic entropy stabilization, and kinetic optimization alone suffice to suppress undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies at grain surfaces and interfaces, thereby enabling efficient charge extraction and minimizing voltage losses—ultimately delivering VOC of 1.0969 V, JSC of 24.113 mA/cm², FF of 69.0619%, and PCE of 18.2667%.
